tickets.title: Contracts generate typed models and enforce the dual-path bid boundary
tickets.objective: packages/contracts: JSON Schemas per DESIGN §Interfaces (partner-reconciled Intent with hard_constraints/preferences, Bid with optional message + seller_asserted provenance, VerificationResult), codegen to Pydantic + TS, and boundary validation: hosted bids reject on any non-hook provenance; external bids admit seller_asserted claims flagged for verification; expired/blacklisted/invalid reject on every path. OpenAPI examples + consumer contract tests for every cross-domain endpoint. Also owns the shared policy contract D13 places in this package: the versioned RankingWeights object the single published rank formula reads its weights, normalization bounds and penalty caps from. The SellerEligibility port is NOT here: amendment 1 (D54) places it in apps/exchange/src/eligibility, owned by T-030, because that is where the amended frozen suite imports it from. Amendment 1 adds two more contracts to this package. (a) The external SigningEnvelope: signer_id, key_id, issued_at, nonce and schema_version are REQUIRED on every Bid submitted through POST /v1/auctions/{auction_id}/bids, plus the single canonical-signing-bytes function over (auction_id, signer_id, store_id, issued_at, nonce, key_id, schema_version, payload_hash) that both signer and verifier call. No optional-field or legacy-tolerant variant exists on the production contract. (b) TrustSnapshot.dims is SIX dimensions - price_honored, discount_honored, shipped_on_time, not_returned, feedback_match, catalog_claim_accuracy - inside one trust system, per D53.
acceptance: 1. Schema→codegen produces importable py+ts types for all pinned objects incl. VerificationResult
2. Hosted-path bid with a seller_asserted claim rejects; external-path bid with the same claim admits flagged-for-verification; expired/blacklisted reject on both
3. Round-trip serialization passes in both languages; every cross-domain endpoint has a checked-in OpenAPI example + contract test

4. RankingWeights is a generated, versioned contract type importable in py+ts, carrying the five published weights, the normalization bounds and the penalty catalogue, and a weight set that does not sum to 1.0 is invalid

5. SigningEnvelope (D52): a Bid missing any one of signer_id/key_id/issued_at/nonce/schema_version fails schema validation in py+ts, and a Bid carrying all five validates - so a schema that rejects everything cannot satisfy this

6. TrustSnapshot carries exactly six dims incl. catalog_claim_accuracy (D53): a six-dim snapshot round-trips in py+ts, a snapshot omitting catalog_claim_accuracy is invalid, and a snapshot naming a seventh dimension is invalid.

tickets.title: Auctions fan out, time out, and always represent every store
tickets.objective: Auction state machine in Redis; POST /auctions; parallel BidRequest fan-out with hard timeout; list-price fallback bids for Tier-0 and non-responding stores (R10). Also creates apps/exchange/src/eligibility (the versioned SellerEligibility port: base class with interface_version and check(store_id) -> EligibilityDecision{store_id, status, reason}, the statuses ELIGIBLE/BLACKLISTED/UNAVAILABLE, and SELLER_ELIGIBILITY_INTERFACE_VERSION) and the apps/exchange/src/orchestration package with the R12 solicitation gate solicit_bids(roster=, solicitor=, eligibility=, now=) -> {solicited, entries, denied}. solicit_bids reads eligibility for every rostered store before any store is asked. The gate sits above collect_bids — collect_bids keeps its (roster, responses, now) parameters and is handed an already-eligible roster.
acceptance: 1. Auction with 3 responsive + 1 silent + 2 Tier-0 stores yields 6 ranked entries, silent one at list price
2. Timeout enforced (frozen clock); late bids rejected
3. State machine transitions logged to ledger via trust API stub

4. Solicitation gate (R12/D54, fail-closed, at the public orchestration boundary, by DENIAL): solicit_bids consults SellerEligibility for every rostered store before fan-out. A BLACKLISTED store, an UNAVAILABLE store and a store whose eligibility read RAISES are each never handed to the solicitor and never appear even as a list-price fallback entry, and each is recorded in the result's denied list with a reason naming its condition. Positive control in the same test: eligible stores ARE solicited in roster order, appear as non-fallback entries, and their solicited prices survive the orchestration layer - so an orchestration that solicits nobody fails here. collect_bids keeps its (roster, responses, now) parameters unchanged and never receives an eligibility argument

tickets.title: Shortlists rank by the single published formula behind eligibility filters
tickets.objective: Eligibility filters (blacklist fail-closed, offer expiry, checkout-domain validity, hard constraints requiring verified facts per R19), then published rank_score per DESIGN §Decisions with [0,1]-normalized features, policy penalties, stable tie-breaking, component map + human-readable explanation; slotting ≤4 with graceful collapse; provenance + verification-warning labels. The eligibility filter is the R12 ranking gate (D54): rank() consults SellerEligibility and excludes the ineligible candidate with a recorded exclusion reason, fail-closed on an unavailable read. Trust inputs are the six-dimension TrustSnapshot (D53); ranking reads the snapshot's score/confidence and never re-derives dimensions.
acceptance: 1. Golden tests: fixed inputs → exact eligibility set, ranking, slots, explanations
2. Blindness test: tier/fee fields cannot alter score; contradicted hard constraint never wins regardless of other components (release blocker test)
3. Filter tests: blacklisted/expired/bad-domain/hard-fail excluded with exclusion_reasons recorded; slots collapse at 1–3 stores

4. Ranking gate + versioned interface (R12/D54, fail-closed, by DENIAL with a positive control): a BLACKLISTED candidate is excluded before any score is computed with its exclusion_reasons entry recorded, an UNAVAILABLE read and a raising read each exclude rather than admit, and the same candidate with an ELIGIBLE verdict IS ranked and CAN win - so a ranker that excludes everything fails. SELLER_ELIGIBILITY_INTERFACE_VERSION is a non-empty string, the three statuses are distinct, and BOTH boundary gates (solicit_bids and accept_offer) refuse an eligibility source whose interface_version is not the published one while accepting one that is

tickets.title: Accepting an offer produces a validated code and permalink
tickets.objective:
Accept endpoint resolves a CheckoutProvider (T-036) by CHECKOUT_MODE and delegates code creation to it, returns the permalink the provider mints, records the accepted event, and handles code-creation failure with re-offer of the next slot. The starting slice runs SimulatedRedirectProvider — the checkout URL is validated against the registered seller domain and checkout_redirect plus the downstream LedgerEvent kinds are emitted identically to the Shopify path (C11); Shopify mode selects the T-052 adapter behind the same port.

CONSTRAINT INHERITED FROM T-030/T-036 (recorded 2026-09-02, load-bearing — do not drop). The checkout host guard compares `offer['checkout_url']` against `bid['store_domain']`, and BOTH come from the SAME store-authored bid — so by itself it rejects only a store that contradicts itself. MEASURED: a bid claiming `store_domain: attacker.tld` with a matching `checkout_url: https://attacker.tld/...` was ADMITTED and minted a real permalink. The T-030 lane added the seam that closes it: `CheckoutRequest.registered_domains`, a platform lookup that overrides the bid outright and FAILS CLOSED on an unknown seller or a raising lookup. It is deliberately NOT wired by default, because the frozen contract at test_spec_criteria.py:1136 pins `bid['store_domain']` and this request is built HERE. **T-033 must pass the platform's registered domain source when constructing CheckoutRequest — a one-line change at this call site.** Until it does, the store's own claim about its domain stands and the guard is decorative.
acceptance: 1. Accept → code+permalink via the resolved provider; ledger events emitted
2. Merchant failure path re-offers deterministically
3. Double-accept on one auction rejected
4. Redirect mode: off-domain checkout_url is refused (release blocker test); emitted event kinds match the Shopify-mode golden sequence

5. Checkout gate (R12/D54, fail-closed, at the public orchestration boundary, by DENIAL): accept_offer(auction=, bid_ref=, code_creator=, mode=, eligibility=) in apps/exchange/src/orchestration RE-READS eligibility at accept time, so a store blacklisted after it bid is refused - no code created (assert the code creator was never called), no permalink, and a denial_reason recorded; an UNAVAILABLE read and a read that RAISES each refuse identically. Positive control in the same test: an ELIGIBLE store with an available read is accepted, mints exactly one code, and returns an on-domain permalink containing that code. accept() keeps its four positional parameters (auction, bid_id, code_creator, mode) and gains no required parameter

tickets.title: Checkout reaches the merchant through a provider port
tickets.objective: apps/exchange/src/checkout: define CheckoutProvider — the single port every accept path goes through to turn a won offer into a discount code and a permalink — and ship SimulatedRedirectProvider as the required starting implementation, which needs no Shopify and no merchant app. Providers register under the CHECKOUT_MODE spellings accept() already resolves ('redirect' and the shopify_stub/shopify spellings); the port, not the provider, performs the registered-domain check, so no implementation can opt out of it, and every provider emits the identical ordered LedgerEvent kinds so nothing downstream can tell which one ran (C11). The Shopify path (T-052) is one adapter behind this port, not the route to a code.
acceptance: 1. CheckoutProvider is one port with a registered provider per CHECKOUT_MODE spelling; resolving an unregistered mode raises rather than silently falling back, and a lint/grep test asserts no code-minting call site exists outside a provider

2. SimulatedRedirectProvider mints a single-use code and an on-domain permalink with no Shopify dependency; the same fixture offer run through the Shopify adapter yields the identical ordered LedgerEvent kinds (C11 parity), so provider swap is invisible downstream

3. The port validates the offer's checkout_url host against the registered seller domain (bid['store_domain']) by exact match BEFORE any provider is asked to mint — rival domain, suffix spoof, glued-suffix spoof, userinfo spoof and subdomain are each refused with no code created (D22); an on-domain offer completes, so a surface that refuses everything cannot satisfy this criterion

4. Provider selection is the mode argument accept() already receives: accept(auction, bid_id, code_creator, mode) keeps its four positional parameters and its injected code creator, and registering a further provider adds no parameter to it

tickets.title: External bids enter signed with a required envelope and route to verification, not rejection
tickets.objective: Signature registration + verification on the external submission door POST /v1/auctions/{auction_id}/bids for non-hosted agents; schema validation admits seller_asserted claims and free-text message, marks the bid unverified, and enqueues extraction+verification carrying the submission's nonce as its idempotency key; hosted solicitation path (POST /v1/bid-requests) unchanged. Amendment 1 (D52) makes the signing envelope REQUIRED, not optional: signer_id, key_id, issued_at, nonce and schema_version are all mandatory and a submission missing any one is Rejected before enqueue. Public surface, all in packages/store_agent/src/external (the module does not move; the exchange route is its only public caller): sign_bid(payload, key); receive_bid(payload, signature, keyring, *, queue, nonce_store, now, auction_deadline, freshness_window_seconds); canonical_signing_bytes(payload) covering auction_id, signer_id, store_id, issued_at, nonce, key_id, schema_version and payload_hash(payload), order-independent and stable across a JSON round trip; NonceStore with seen(signer_id, nonce) and purge_expired(as_of). The keyring is {signer_id: {key_id: secret}} backed by app.seller_endpoints so keys rotate; an unknown (signer_id, key_id) pair rejects rather than falling back to another key of that signer, and a lookup keyed on key_id alone is wrong because two signers may reuse a key_id string.
acceptance: 1. Registered-key signed external bid carrying a complete envelope is accepted, marked unverified, and enqueued exactly once with the nonce as the queued item's idempotency key; a bad signature rejects and enqueues nothing. The positive case must pass, so a receiver that rejects everything fails this criterion
2. Hosted bid with non-hook provenance still rejects (regression)
3. Expired/blacklisted external bids reject before enqueue

4. Required envelope (D52): five submissions, each omitting exactly one of signer_id, key_id, issued_at, nonce, schema_version, are each rejected before enqueue; the otherwise-identical submission carrying all five is accepted

5. Canonical bytes and coverage (D52): canonical_signing_bytes is deterministic, independent of mapping insertion order and stable across a JSON round trip; payload_hash is a digest of at least 32 chars that changes when the offer body changes and appears inside the canonical bytes; mutating any of auction_id, signer_id, store_id, issued_at, nonce, key_id, schema_version or the offer body changes the bytes; and tampering with any of them after signing rejects at the door

6. Key rotation (D52): a signer with two live key_id rows verifies under either; a signature naming an unregistered key_id for a known signer rejects with no fallback to that signer's other key; and a second signer reusing the first signer's key_id string under a different secret does not verify - so a lookup keyed on key_id alone fails

7. Replay and freshness (D52): resubmitting an accepted payload rejects; a different nonce from the same signer is still accepted and the same nonce from a DIFFERENT signer is accepted (scoping is per signer); NonceStore.seen stays True after purge_expired at any moment before the auction deadline and becomes False only after it passes; a submission arriving after the auction deadline rejects; and an issued_at outside freshness_window_seconds rejects in both directions, far-past and clock-skewed-future

tickets.title: A conformance gate keeps the two JCS canonicalizers from drifting
tickets.objective: ORCHESTRATOR RULING (cycle 2, user-delegated): keep both RFC-8785 implementations and make divergence impossible, rather than unifying them. D16's letter — 'Nothing outside apps/trust/src/ledger/** (T-011) defines its own hashing' — is unachievable as written: it asks for one definition owned by the ledger, but packages/contracts is the schema foundation every service imports and apps/trust is an app, so a package cannot import from it and the reverse edge is architecturally wrong. D16 is also already violated on main: T-010's signing.py defines hashing outside the ledger. The two implementations AGREE byte-for-byte today (~1.5M inputs, both on the RFC 3.1 predicate float(v)==v), so the live risk is future drift, not present divergence. A shared conformance gate closes that at near-zero risk; unification would additionally remove duplication, which is real but marginal, while touching a security boundary that just had two CRITICALs fixed. Build the gate. Unification stays available later and is not owed.
acceptance: 1. A conformance test drives packages/contracts/tests/canonicalization_corpus.json plus the RFC 8785 3.2.4 worked example through BOTH Python canonicalizers in ONE process and asserts byte-identical output

2. It also covers the classes where independent implementations diverge: integers at and past 2**53/2**63/2**64, 10**16, 10**23, 10**400, -0, exponent-form switchovers at 1e21 and 1e-7, lone surrogates in keys AND values, UTF-16 vs code-point key ordering with non-BMP keys, and an NFC pair (neither may normalize)
3. Both implementations agree on WHICH inputs they refuse, not merely on what they render — a refusal on one side and a render on the other is a failure
4. It lives in e2e/ (in the root testpaths, importable from both) and runs in the ordinary suite, so `make verify` catches drift
5. Reverting either implementation's number predicate to a safe-integer bound turns the gate RED

Do NOT amend D16

tickets.title: The .pkgroot namespaces survive a pytest run (root cause: site-packages itself is flagged)
tickets.objective:
`_proxyshop.pth` in the primary checkout keeps reverting to macOS UF_HIDDEN, which `site.addpackage` silently skips, so every .pkgroot flat namespace (contracts, llm, trust, ...) becomes unimportable outside pytest. This has now bitten the run THREE times and cost two false metric readings (acceptance_pass_rate 5.00 instead of 13.33 at cycle 1; build_succeeds 1->0 twice). WHAT IS ESTABLISHED, measured: a bare `python -c` run does NOT re-hide it; `pytest --version` DOES; `pytest --collect-only --noconftest` did NOT; importing pytest, proxyshop_support, or any of conftest's eight imports individually does NOT. Those results are mutually inconsistent, so the deterministic trigger is NOT isolated and this ticket must not pretend otherwise — an earlier orchestrator claim that the root conftest.py was responsible is RETRACTED. WHAT IS CERTAIN: it recurs, it correlates with pytest invocations, and bootstrap.sh:26-33's one-shot `chflags nohidden ... || true` is a reset that decays and cannot fail loudly. The durable fix is to stop depending on the flag: assert the effect immediately before every measurement, and make anything that spawns a child hand it .pkgroot explicitly (see T-122, the same class).

FURTHER EVIDENCE (cycle 5, orchestrator + watchdog, jointly): the watchdog ran nine probes (bare python, import pytest, import _pytest.config, pytest --version with and without plugin autoload, python -m pytest --version, import uv, a read-only ls) and NONE re-hid the flag; it also refuted the uv theory in an isolated scratch venv (uv 0.11.8 venv + editable install leaves site-packages and both .pth files at flags '-'). So it is NOT uv and NOT pytest in isolation. On the orchestrator's side `pytest --version` DOES re-hide, and it reproduces with no concurrent bootstrap running, so the concurrent-writer hypothesis does not explain it either. The datum that reframes it: the site-packages DIRECTORY itself carries UF_HIDDEN, and so do ALL THREE .pth files (_proxyshop, _virtualenv, a1_coverage) — not just ours. That is a directory-level property, which is why `chflags nohidden` on a single file is fragile. Trigger still NOT isolated; the two sessions' results genuinely disagree and neither has been able to make the other's reproduce.

RESOLVED, cycle 5. The site-packages DIRECTORY carried UF_HIDDEN, not merely the .pth files, so `chflags nohidden <one file>` was always a partial repair that appeared to 'come back'. A RECURSIVE clear holds: after `chflags -R nohidden .venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages`, the flag survives `pytest --version`, survives a full `pytest packages/llm` suite, and a bare `python -c "import contracts, llm, trust"` succeeds AFTERWARDS. Measured, all four states. This also explains why the two sessions could not reproduce each other: the outcome depends on the directory's flag, which differed between the venvs each was probing. bootstrap.sh:26-33 should clear the directory as well as the file, and assert the effect loudly instead of `|| true`.

METHOD NOTE worth keeping, from both sessions' post-mortem: the directory flag was OBSERVED and REPORTED before either session used it — the follow-up bisect still cleared a single file, so nine 'clean' probes were partial repairs producing evidence about the method rather than about the trigger. Having a datum is not the same as designing the next experiment against it. What actually resolved this was each session running the check that could FALSIFY its own position: the uv refutation killed one theory, the flag-cleared test run killed the other. Neither defended.
acceptance: 1. A pytest run in the primary checkout leaves the .pkgroot namespaces importable by a bare child afterwards, or the provisioning asserts and repairs the flag immediately before each measurement
2. The assertion fails LOUDLY rather than warning — bootstrap.sh:48-51 currently ends in `|| echo WARNING >&2`
3. A regression test proves a bare `python -c "import contracts, llm, trust"` succeeds after a full pytest run
4. If the trigger is found, name it; if not, say so and defend the mitigation on its own terms
5. Whatever mitigation is chosen must survive a full pytest run, proven by a bare `python -c` import AFTER the suite, not before

6. bootstrap.sh:26-33 clears the flag RECURSIVELY on site-packages (it currently iterates one path and ends `|| true`, so it can neither cover the directory nor report failing), and then ASSERTS THE EFFECT — import one namespace, print its resolved path, fail loudly if it raises. This is the same 'assert the effect, never the exit code' rule this run already applies to installers, applied to the one provisioning step that was exempt from it.

tickets.title: Rotating pseudonyms are trivially re-linkable, so T-070's central guarantee does not hold
tickets.objective:
DECISION MADE (user, 2026-09-02): amend the frozen contract. Note the amendment number is now 4, not 3 — a separate amendment 3 (build_succeeds logging) landed on main at f65816a.

[HIGH] T-070's objective is 'rotating pseudonyms, identity-free profiles'. The rotation is real but it buys nothing: `buckets` is a PURE FUNCTION OF THE ACCOUNT, so successive pseudonyms publish BYTE-IDENTICAL profiles. MEASURED by the T-070 lane: 3 rotations produced 3 distinct pseudonyms and ONE identical bucket set. Any store that has seen a buyer once re-links every later pseudonym of that buyer, which is precisely the linkage the feature exists to prevent. The pseudonym rotates; the fingerprint underneath it does not.

Contributing, from the same lane: `coarsen_categories` passes order-category free text through with a count cap but NO length or vocabulary cap. That free-text slug is the high-entropy half of the linkage — a bucket set drawn from a closed vocabulary is far less identifying than one carrying arbitrary category strings.

WHY IT NEEDS A DECISION: closing it requires suppression or k-anonymity on `BuyerProfile`, which changes the profile contract the frozen acceptance tests pin. Options are (a) amend the frozen contract (user-approved amendment, as with ESC-002), (b) accept the linkage and downgrade the objective's claim so the docs stop promising unlinkability, or (c) a scheme that preserves the pinned shape while breaking linkage. Do not dispatch until one is chosen.

=== AMENDMENT DESIGN v1: REFUTED, DO NOT APPLY AS SPECIFIED (2026-09-02) ===
Full spec + all four refutations: .swarm-loop/reports/T-132-amendment-design-REFUTED.json

A 13-agent design pass (5 designs, 3 judges, synthesis, 4 adversarial skeptics) produced a PURELY ADDITIVE amendment: 4 new tests, 120 -> 124, zero relaxations. It established one genuinely useful fact by EXECUTION: **the frozen contract does not block the fix at all.** `ProfileBuckets` already types every facet optional and the frozen pins constrain KEYS and TYPES only, so a generalisation fix is entirely a change of VALUES that both frozen T-070 tests are blind to (2 passed before, 2 passed after a prototype fix). The T-070 lane's claim that fixing this 'changes a contract the frozen acceptance pins' was WRONG.

3 of 4 skeptics cleared it; mechanics verified (anchors unique, exactly +4 collected, both frozen T-070 tests byte-identical, 6 sabotages caught). THE FOURTH REFUTED IT BY CONSTRUCTION, with measurements rather than argument, and it is right:

[CRITICAL] A degenerate `build_buckets` passes all 4 new tests AND both frozen T-070 tests (6 passed) while leaving buyers essentially as re-linkable as the shipped defect. The k floor is measured ONLY against the 30-account `_reference_population()` baked into the test file, and that fixture exercises a tiny corner of the domain: 3 budget bands, 3 frequency tiers (max 9 orders, so 'frequent' is never reached), 3 countries, 2 category strings per buyer. Every value OUTSIDE that window is unconstrained — so an implementation generalises exactly where the fixture looks and fingerprints everywhere else.

[CRITICAL] The amendment's own GREEN reference implementation DOES NOT DELIVER the guarantee it certifies: measured on 4,000 buyers it leaves 2787 equivalence classes and 58.2% uniquely identified. So passing says almost nothing about the property — not merely that a cheat can pass, but that a green run is not evidence for the claim its own failure messages make.

[HIGH] Each bypass is an ORDINARY PARTIAL IMPLEMENTATION, not a contrived hardcode — 'we only have region rollup tables for our launch markets', 'keep the exact order count for high-volume buyers', 'hash unrecognised categories into the vocabulary'. Measured, each passing the amended suite: honest 58.2% uniquely identified; region-variant 78.3% unique / 95.3% in a crowd < 5; band-variant 78.4% unique / 89.1% in a crowd < 5.

[HIGH] The `first_time` redundancy claim is not established: a plugin setting `first_time = (not orders) or bool(account.get('loyalty_id'))` passes, because no fixture account carries `loyalty_id`. In production that is an unsuppressible extra bit that splits every k-class.

[MEDIUM] CATEGORY_AFFINITY_MAX=3 drawn from CATEGORY_VOCABULARY_MAX=24 admits 2,325 distinct affinity sets; the constant's own docstring rejects 8-of-24 as 'a fingerprint again' but never applies that arithmetic to the limit it actually sets. Nothing bounds the JOINT entropy.

[MEDIUM] The 200-account sweep asserts only that the vocabulary did not grow — nothing about the 200 values it published.

REQUIRED REPAIR before v2 is applied:
  1. Assert the JOINT quantity over a GENERATED population spanning the full domain, not a hand-built 30-account fixture: both `min(class size) >= K` AND `len(classes) <= len(population) // K`. That is the only assertion shape that forces coarsening everywhere rather than where the fixture looks, and it bounds joint entropy directly.
  2. Close the vocabulary for region, budget_band and frequency_tier too — not just category_affinity. This alone kills three of the four measured channels.
  3. Assert `first_time` redundancy DIRECTLY (`first_time == (frequency_tier == ZERO_ORDER_TIER)`) rather than inferring it from one unequal pair.
  4. Add the three ordinary-partial-implementation variants as REQUIRED sabotage checks; the existing five all publish nothing, publish a constant, add noise, self-intern, or leave region wholly untouched — none has this shape.

tickets.title: A replayer can relabel a signed delivery onto a topic of its choice AND destroy the genuine one. handle_delivery takes the topic from the UNSIGNED URL path when the X-Shopify-Topic header is absent (`topic = topic or wanted`), while WebhookInbox de-duplicates on the body digest alone (webhooks.py:223-238). The class docstring explicitly raises this exact threat -- 'one captured signed body replay as three distinct fresh events -- a paid order becoming a fabricated fulfilment and a fabricated refund' -- and claims the body-only key defeats it. It defeats the three-events variant only. The one-event-relabelled variant works, and it is worse than a duplicate: it consumes the identity, so the real delivery is swallowed.

The shipped exchange denies every store and represents none, which is the exact inverse of the R10 property the branch is claimed to deliver; it also silently runs on InMemoryAuctionStore and an InMemoryLedgerSink that is discarded per process, so the DESIGN-pinned `auction:{id}` Redis record with its 15-minute TTL and the ledger trail are never written by any deployment.

tickets.title: A connection failure never becomes a StoreUnavailable, so an unreachable or restarting Postgres returns HTTP 500 with an empty body after a 30-second block, instead of the 503 store_unavailable the module documents. `_connection()` obtains the connection OUTSIDE the try/except in `_append_on`, and `classify_write_error` (pg.py:91) only maps psycopg.errors raised by the INSERT itself. `psycopg_pool.PoolTimeout` and `psycopg.OperationalError` are not EventServiceError subclasses, so `routes._refuse` (routes.py:98) never sees them and the handler raises. Only the no-DSN path reaches StoreUnavailable. errors.py:83 promises '503 - nothing is wrong with the request' and routes.py:216 argues that /events/verify must always answer because 'a 5xx here would be indistinguishable from the verifier being down - which is precisely the state an attacker who had just tampered with the ledger would like it to be confused with'. A down database produces exactly that confusion. The 30 s block is psycopg_pool's default timeout, so with Starlette's 40-thread sync pool ~40 concurrent requests wedge the whole trust service. No test covers it: the only 503 assertion in the 87-test suite is the scorer-unavailable one at test_events.py:1174.

tickets.title: MAX_SWEEP_DEPTH = 12 truncates the provenance walk SILENTLY. A priced node, a claim, or a discount nested 13+ levels deep in a dict-shaped bid is admitted having been inspected by nothing. This bypasses EVERY boundary wall — the claim provenance walk, the floor wall and the new price reconciliation alike — not merely the price checks, so it is strictly wider than the T-153 defect that surfaced it. Raising the bound does not fix it, and refusing everything past the bound would refuse an honestly deep metadata blob, which _sweep is explicitly written to tolerate. The bound's stated purpose is to stop a self-referential dict hanging the boundary, so the correct fix is CYCLE DETECTION replacing the depth bound.

tickets.title: The one-accept-per-auction guard is only as durable as the record handed in. accept() stamps the auction OBJECT it receives. A route that loads an AuctionRecord from RedisAuctionStore, accepts, and does not save it back leaves an unstamped record for the next request; and two concurrent requests reading it can both pass the guard, because the check-then-act window spans the whole provider call including merchant I/O. The durable guard belongs on AuctionStateMachine's already-serialised ACCEPTED transition.

tickets.title: CONFIRMS THE build_succeeds FALSE-ZERO MECHANISM. The D37 cross-worker Neo4j flock can never complete a contended wait and its own loud failure is unreachable: _neo4j_guard takes the lock during session-fixture setup, pytest-timeout covers setup, and 300 < 600, so pytest always kills the test first. Under contention `make verify` ERRORS and build_succeeds is recorded 0, with a traceback naming neither Neo4j nor the lock unless you read the frame. The lock is machine-global (/tmp/proxyshop-neo4j.lock) and shared across worktrees, so a swarm makes contention the normal case. This is very likely the cause of the four historical false zeros on build_succeeds, and of two non-reproducing flakes observed this cycle. Supersedes/sharpens T-171.

tickets.title: THE TWO DOORS DO NOT RUN THE SAME SCHEMA CHECK — 21 measured ok-divergences. TypeScript validates through ajv WITH ajv-formats, so `format: date-time` is enforced on all eight timestamp fields; Python validates through the generated pydantic models where every one of those fields is a bare `str`, so the format keyword is unenforced. Separately, the docstring claim that both read blacklisted truthily 'the same way' is false for empty containers: Python's bool([]) is False while JavaScript's [] is truthy, so blacklisted: [] is ADMITTED by Python and REFUSED by TypeScript. tickets.title: ClaimMaterial gained a fifth field, `unwalkable`, as part of the T-155 cycle-detection fix (a cycle or an unwalkably-deep structure is now NAMED rather than silently pruned, which is the whole point — a boundary that quietly stops walking is reporting on a structure it was not handed). It is accessed by name everywhere in-tree, so nothing in this repo breaks, but any consumer unpacking it POSITIONALLY would. Recorded so a future integrator does not discover it by breakage. Two behaviours also tightened, both strictly fail-closed, and a caller should know: enforce_bid_provenance now REFUSES a self-referential or unwalkably-deep bid rather than truncating it, and authorize_discount now DENIES (REASON_UNPRICEABLE_PRODUCT) for a catalog entry whose list_price is unreadable, rather than granting at a phantom list price of 0.00.

tickets.title: SECOND INDEPENDENT SIGHTING, on a different worker, which changes the diagnosis. tickets.title: TWO CORRECTIONS, ONE OF THEM TO MY OWN ASSERTION. (1) I claimed the chflags window could corrupt a metric read. THAT IS WRONG, measured: a pytest run is IMMUNE to the hidden window because pytest's `pythonpath` ini re-adds .pkgroot — `pytest packages/llm` -> 210 passed, `mypy` -> Success, and `make demo-seed`'s child -> OK, all INSIDE the open window. So T-174 does not explain a false build_succeeds zero through `make verify`; it breaks service entry points and bare imports only. That immunity is also why it survived six cycles with nothing going red. My T-174 record should be read with this correction attached. (2) The real cause stands and is NOT fixed: a Neo4jLockTimeout is still a non-zero `make verify`, so build_succeeds is STILL recorded 0 for a machine condition. Lowering the lock 600->240 makes that zero diagnosable and correctly attributed; it does not stop it happening, and it converts waits of 241-295s from success into failure. The cure is scheduler-level and therefore MINE: never run a measurement concurrently with a lane that touches the graph, or measure in a quiesced tree. The repo's own doctrine rules out the obvious alternative — skipping instead of failing would be invisible in the metrics.

tickets.title: THE InvalidSchemaName FLAKE HAS ONE MECHANISM AND IT IS NEITHER OF THE TWO I RECORDED. T-196 called it order-dependence; T-201 called it cross-lane collision on a worker database. tickets.title: make verify fails the types gate with 8 mypy errors across 3 store-agent modules merged in cycle 14, holding build_succeeds at 0 and blocking the epoch push. All 8 are UNSOUND ANNOTATIONS over CORRECT runtime behaviour, and each has a narrowing fix that makes the type system state the invariant the code already enforces. (a) modes/runner.py:317 - rationale_for() dispatches on is_decline(answer), a plain bool predicate mypy cannot narrow, so Bid|Decline is passed to _decline_clauses(Decline) and _offer_clauses(Bid); the repair is to give is_decline a TypeGuard[Decline] return type. (b) external/door.py:271,328 - signer_id/nonce/key_id are read with payload.get() (Any|None) and passed to keyring_secret(str,str) and NonceStore.consume(str,str); they cannot be None on that path because step 2 calls canonical_signing_bytes(payload), which raises CanonicalisationError unless missing_signing_fields() finds every one of REQUIRED_SIGNING_FIELDS to be a non-blank str (signing.py:315-336, 351-356) - the repair is to carry the VALIDATED envelope values forward from the canonicalization step instead of re-reading raw payload.get(), so the type reflects the guard that is already there. (c) learning/state.py:216-217 - the loop variable name 'tally' is reused: bound first to DepthTally over learned.depths, then rebound to Tally over learned.commitments (ClusterLearning declares commitments: tuple[Tally,...] at state.py:99, and Tally carries .label), so mypy keeps the first binding's type; the repair is to rename the second loop variable.

tickets.title: ENVELOPE VERSION HISTORY IS PROCESS-LOCAL AND DIES WITH THE PROCESS. EnvelopeVersions keeps append-only history, version-never-backwards and activate-the-head in memory (ENVELOPES = EnvelopeVersions() at module level), in the same spirit as merchant_svc.collector.PIXEL_INBOX. DESIGN puts the real history in sealed.envelopes (versioned, no grant for the exchange role). Losing it can only STOP a store bidding, never start one, so the failure mode is the safe one — but the three invariants are lost at the persistence boundary unless a migration carries them. Reported by the T-053 lane as a known limitation of what it could build inside its ownership, not as an oversight.

tickets.title: EXTENDS T-229 FROM 3 FIELDS TO 6, MEASURED. The rung-2 verifier for cycle 15 batch 1 confirmed T-229 and widened it: _work_item (door.py:191-206) re-reads the payload for ALL SIX identity fields, not the three T-228 hardened. With a Mapping that answers honestly for the first N reads of one key and then lies (swap_after=7), receive_bid returns accepted=True while the enqueued work item carries the attacker's value for auction_id, store_id, issued_at, nonce, signer_id and key_id. The door spends the honest nonce in its replay memory while enqueueing the attacker's nonce as the documented idempotency key, so the replay memory and the downstream dedup key disagree — precisely the hazard the new gate-2b comment says matters most at the nonce. Exploitability is currently ZERO because receive_bid has no production callers.

tickets.title: THE SIMULATION VALIDATES ONLY HALF ITS OWN LEDGER, AND THE HALF IT SKIPS CONTAINS THE EXACT DEFECT CLASS THE SIM EXISTS TO CATCH. runner.py:727 validates raw_events only, fed solely from the accept path (runner.py:661). The auction state machine writes to a SEPARATE ledger_sink (runner.py:559-560) that is never read and never validated. tickets.title: A caller-supplied NaN still produces an UNAUTHENTICATED HTTP 500. list_price: NaN and tier: 1e400 both return 500. Pre-existing rather than a regression, but the batch's own test docstring asserts 'Nothing the caller can write may produce a 5xx', which is measurably false on merged main. Note the F1 fix (allow_inf_nan=False) does NOT close this -- it makes NaN a rejection, and rejection is exactly the path that 500s.

tickets.title: A TOTAL try/except Exception ERODES THE GATE IT WAS MEANT TO SATISFY. receive_bid (door.py:358) is now a thin catch-all wrapper around _receive_bid (door.py:410): the try at :386 and `except Exception` at :401 return _refuse(REASON_DOOR_FAILED_CLOSED, payload=payload) at :407 for ANY escaping exception. The test that grades this property, packages/store-agent/tests/test_repro_external_door.py:398 test_the_door_never_raises_on_the_three_inputs_that_make_it_raise, only asserts that each of its three hostile inputs returns with `accepted is not True` (:470-479). With the catch-all in place that assertion is satisfied by the wrapper alone, so the test can no longer distinguish 'each of the three inputs is handled by name inside _receive_bid' -- which is what its own docstring at :401-416 enumerates (the overflowing freshness_window_seconds, the blacklist whose __iter__ raises, and _refuse re-reading the payload it is refusing) -- from 'everything is swallowed at the outer frame'. If any of the three named fixes regresses, the test stays green. The wrapper is the right belt-and-braces (an anonymous POST must never 500), but it must not be the only thing holding the property up: the three inner fixes need assertions that see BELOW the wrapper -- e.g. driving _receive_bid directly, or asserting the refusal REASON is the by-name one rather than door_failed_closed.

tickets.title: AN EXCEPTION ON A PATH WHOSE STATED CONTRACT IS 'NEVER FAIL THE AUCTION'. build_published_event (apps/exchange/src/auction/ledger.py:118) raises MalformedLedgerPayload at :148 when a body is missing a published key. Both of its consumers are on paths that cannot absorb that. (a) SUCCESS PATH: apps/exchange/src/checkout/provider.py:842 calls self._events(...) inside the try opened at :827, whose `except Exception as exc` at :851 raises OrphanedCheckoutCode at :858 -- so a malformed AUDIT RECORD turns a SUCCESSFULLY MINTED, live discount code into a refusal handed back to the buyer. The handler's own comment at :852-856 says it exists because 'building the result cannot normally fail'; build_published_event made that assumption false by adding a validating raise inside the region it guards. (b) REFUSAL PATH: apps/exchange/src/accept/offer.py:294 (_orphan_record) and :359 (the policy_event) both call build_published_event from inside _refused, which accept() at :393 invokes from the `except Exception as exc` handler at :496-514. A raise inside an except block propagates out of accept() uncaught -- there is no outer try in accept() -- so a malformed orphan body becomes a 500 on the refusal path, on precisely the input the orphan machinery exists to record. LATENT TODAY, which is why this is a ticket and not a fix now: both call sites currently pass every published key (provider.py:1011-1013 for code_created; offer.py:300-302 for the orphan record), so nothing reaches the raise. It is one dropped key away from a live discount being refused to a buyer or a 500 on the refusal path. The repair is at the CONSUMERS -- report the malformed body, do not let it decide the auction -- not by weakening the producing-boundary check T-235 was closed with.

  {"accepted": false, "denial_reason": "checkout_refused: CheckoutCreatorError: injected code creator <object object at 0x102f49d00> exposes neither create_code(...) nor __call__(...)"}

tickets.title: THE ACCEPT PATH T-170 JUST SHIPPED CANNOT ACCEPT ANYTHING, BECAUSE NOTHING IN THE REPOSITORY PERSISTS AN AUCTION'S BIDS. `AuctionRecord` (apps/exchange/src/auction/state.py:100) carries `roster` and has no `bids` field at all. `POST /auctions` calls `solicit_bids` at auction/routes.py:288, renders `result.entries` into the response at :307 via `_entries_out`, and drops the collected `BidEntry` list -- `machine.close` at :302 only stamps `closed_at`/`history`. The accept route reads bids through the injected `app.state.auction_bids` port whose default, `NoRecordedBids` (accept/routes.py:110), knows nothing, so `accept()` -> `_find_bid` -> `_bids_of` (accept/offer.py:202) gets an empty sequence and refuses every accept with `unknown_bid`. The two halves are already built and simply not connected: `InMemoryAuctionBids.record(auction_id, bids)` exists at accept/routes.py:136 and `configure_accept(..., bids=...)` at accept/routes.py:177/211. The fix is one `record(auction_id, [entry.bid for entry in result.entries])` after auction/routes.py:288 plus wiring the same store into `configure_accept(bids=...)`. THE WRONG FIX, EXPLICITLY: do NOT rebuild bids from `roster`. `RosterEntry` (auction/routes.py:94, fields at :138-169) carries `list_price` and NO `store_domain`, so an accept built from a roster row would (a) hand the buyer a discount computed against a price the store never offered, and (b) leave the registered-domain check with no domain to check -- re-opening T-169 through the back door. The C18-accept lane documented this gap in its own module docstring (accept/routes.py:34-44) and reported it in NEEDS rather than fixing it, because auction/routes.py was outside its scope. NO TICKET OWNS IT: a search of all 240 tickets for `auction_bids`, `NoRecordedBids`, `unknown_bid`, and AuctionRecord-plus-bids returns zero hits.

Its exchange-side gate, apps/exchange/tests/test_repro_open_tickets.py::test_t204_a_denial_reason_is_drawn_from_a_declared_vocabulary, now PASSES -- the C18-accept merge added `exchange.accept.DENIAL_REASONS` (already_accepted, auction_not_acceptable, blacklisted, checkout_refused, unavailable, unknown_bid, unrecordable_acceptance, unspecified), which is what that test's `_declared_denial_vocabulary()` helper accepts. Its contracts-side gate, packages/contracts/tests/test_repro_open_tickets.py::test_the_published_denial_reason_has_an_enumerated_vocabulary, is STILL xfail(strict=True) at merged main: line 169 is a bare {"type": "string"} with no `enum`. So T-204's verify command answers green while half its own gate is red, and a collector reading only the verify would mark it done. This is a reporting hazard, not a new defect -- T-204 (open) owns the enum, so do NOT mint a duplicate for it. (2) THE TWO LINES ARE COUPLED and no ticket says so: the contracts gate asserts BOTH that `enum` is truthy AND that the document's `example` is a member of it. Line 172's example is `"blacklist"`, and the vocabulary's term is `"blacklisted"` -- so adding the enum alone leaves that gate red on its second assertion. Line 172 is T-267's defect. Whoever closes T-204 must change 169 and 172 in the same edit or the strict gate stays red. (3) T-267's SECOND ASSERTION IS FALSE: it states "NOTHING IN THE REPO READS THIS FILE: no test, no codegen, no script", and therefore that the document "can drift arbitrarily from the implementation with nothing detecting it". Measured at merged main, ten tracked files reference exchange.openapi.json, including packages/contracts/src/ts/openapi.ts, packages/contracts/src/openapi.py, apps/buyer/svc/src/accept/handoff.py and errors.py, and four test files -- packages/contracts/tests/test_openapi_contracts.py and both test_repro_open_tickets.py files assert on it. SECONDARY, and NOT redundant: a runtime probe that materialises the COPY set and imports each shipped module, which covers the one case the static check cannot -- a module that IS shipped but broken for another reason (syntax, an import side effect, a missing third-party dep). tickets.title: THE SYSTEM HAS NO OBSERVABILITY AT ALL, AND EVERY INFO-LEVEL CALL IS SILENTLY DISCARDED. tickets.title: THE REPRODUCTION-GATE IDIOM HAS A STRUCTURAL BLIND SPOT THAT ONLY DISAPPEARS WHEN THE DEFECT IS FIXED, AND IT SHOULD BE STATED WHEREVER THE IDIOM IS RECOMMENDED. While a gate is an xfail(strict=True) latch over N known failures, a NEW failure of the same kind joins the N inside the latch and the run's exit code does not change — measured here: sabotages that made a runbook step vanish or a missing script pass returned ordinary rc=0, byte-identical to baseline but for timings. The lane that found this correctly REFUSED to 'fix' it by pinning the current failure count, because pinning today's failures pins the defect. The resolution is not a code change: once the underlying defect is fixed and the marker comes off, a newly-broken step reddens a plain run on its own. So the blind spot is real, is inherent to the idiom, and is self-closing — but during the window where a gate is red-and-latched, that gate cannot detect a SECOND defect of its own kind, and nothing anywhere says so.

Closure (a) should therefore assert the key it reserves UNDER, not just that a single SET .. NX is issued; that covers reservation_key too and is a cheap addition to a test being written anyway.

At the symbol level `reserve` is NOT only-conditionally covered: one conditional test and four unconditional ones reference that name. That does not weaken this ticket -- it CONFIRMS its central sentence, because the unconditional four exercise a DIFFERENT IMPLEMENTATION of the same method name (the file-backed stand-in), not the Redis one the deployment runs. Anyone auditing with a symbol-level tool will see '5 tests cover reserve' and conclude this ticket is wrong; they are counting a name, not a code path.

CLASS CONTEXT, so the severity is not over-read: 53 production symbols in this repo are exercised only by environment-conditional tests, and essentially all of the others are Neo4j- or Postgres-backed code in services/ingest/src/graph/ and apps/trust/src/ledger/, where docker-only coverage is INHERENT because the behaviour under test is the datastore's. tickets.title: THE ENVELOPE TABLE CAN PERSIST AN ACTIVATION THE DOMAIN RULE FORBIDS, so activation cannot cross the persistence boundary. sealed.envelopes declares store_id, version, activation, max_discount_pct, budget_cap, floors, pursue_clusters, standing_commitments, created_at and NOTHING ELSE -- there is no column for the approval artifact. Its CHECK constraint envelopes_activation_check accepts activation IN ('shadow','active','killed'), so a row asserting 'active' with no recorded approval is valid at the storage layer. That is exactly the state T-248 establishes must be refused in memory (record() must reject a caller-asserted activation='active' with approval=None), so the two layers now disagree: the domain rule forbids what the schema permits. Consequence today, reported by the lane that built the durability seam: a row read back as 'active' has to be restored in SHADOW and logged at WARNING, because the artifact that would justify activation cannot be stored. The direction is deliberately fail-safe -- a restart can only stop a store bidding, never start one -- but it means an approved, activated envelope silently loses its activation across a restart, and R6's requirement that a live envelope carry the approval that authorized it cannot be satisfied durably at all. TWO FURTHER LIMITS OF THE SAME SCHEMA, from the same measurement: there is no ordering column and activate()/kill() do not bump the version, while envelopes_pkey is (store_id, version) -- so the durable side can hold only each version's CURRENT state while the transition log lives in memory and dies with the process. Nothing in the ticket graph owns any of this: T-239 is the nearest ticket and it is the durability seam itself, now fixed, not the schema it writes into.

That line reads: 'No k-anonymity enforcement beyond a configurable floor (default 1 in fixtures; production knob documented).' The default-1 half is correct and deliberate -- it is a stated NON-GOAL, it is what the fixtures pin, and cycle-9 already ruled that calling it a defect was wrong. The 'production knob documented' half is not met: PROXYSHOP_BUYER_K_ANONYMITY appears nowhere in .env.example, README.md or docs/ -- the grep is silent across all three. So an operator deploying this has no way to learn that the floor exists, that it defaults to 1, or how to raise it. Split out of T-221, which was ruled invalid because its core claim (that the default-1 floor is itself a defect) contradicts the SPEC non-goal and a prior ruling; this is the residue of that ticket that IS real. Deliberately scoped to documentation: the knob itself exists and works, and no code change is wanted here. Note for whoever takes it that raising the floor above 1 is not a safe default to recommend casually -- anonymise_cohort raises ValueError when len(accounts) < floor, so a single-account profile build under a floor > 1 returns a 500, which means the documentation must say what the knob costs as well as what it does.

tickets.title: POST /pixel/collect is unauthenticated BY DESIGN and its body IS capped at 1 MiB by read_capped_body - that part is correct. What is unbounded is the length of any FIELD inside it: _scalar() checks the TYPE only (str/int/float) and returns value.strip() with no length check. Those uncapped strings land in a 512-entry ring, so the store is bounded and the per-entry size is not, and the resulting ceiling is LARGER THAN THE CONTAINER. Separable second half: the accept path writes observation.checkout_token verbatim into a _log.info, and a log has no capacity, so that half is linear and unbounded in aggregate - contradicting the module's own rule 30 lines above that an error body is as much a place data lives as a database is. The refusal path honours that rule; the accept path does not.

tickets.title: MEASUREMENT-CREDIBILITY HAZARD: any agent or engineer measuring a scratch copy of this repo silently measures the WRONG TREE unless they know one specific trick, and the failure reports as a clean green. pyproject.toml sets pythonpath = ['.', '.pkgroot'], which pytest inserts at sys.path[0] AFTER the interpreter has honoured PYTHONPATH. So the conventional isolation technique - prefix PYTHONPATH with the scratch copy - is silently defeated: the real worktree shadows the copy, the sabotage never executes, and the run reports PASSED. TWO INDEPENDENT AGENTS were fooled by this in a single session; each caught it only because it had planted an explicit witness file, and one of them reported a reassuring '23 passed' and the other '38 passed' before noticing. Every sabotage, mutation test and both-ways proof in this repo rests on getting this right, so a false green here invalidates the evidence for a fix rather than merely wasting time. Known working alternatives, both measured: pass -o "pythonpath=<shim> . .pkgroot" so the shim precedes the repo entries, or rebind the package's __path__ before import.
